input.summary:
Implemented a complete in-memory Task Management API in TypeScript using only Node.js built-in modules. Here's what was built:

## File Structure
- **src/types.ts** — All TypeScript interfaces: `User`, `Project`, `Task`, `Comment`, `Notification`, `TaskStatus`, and HTTP helper types (`RouteHandler`, `ParsedRequest`, `ResponseHelper`, `Route`)
- **src/store.ts** — Singleton in-memory store using `Map<string, T>` for all five entity types
- **src/utils.ts** — Helper utilities: `generateId()` (using `crypto.randomUUID`), `now()` (ISO timestamp), `createNotification()`
- **src/router.ts** — Custom HTTP router with pattern-based route matching (`:param` wildcards), JSON body parsing, and a `ResponseHelper` abstraction
- **src/handlers/users.ts** — CRUD handlers with email uniqueness enforcement
- **src/handlers/projects.ts** — CRUD handlers with member add/remove and cascade-delete of tasks & comments
- **src/handlers/tasks.ts** — CRUD handlers with strict status transitions (`todo → in-progress → done`), filtering by projectId, assignment with notifications
- **src/handlers/comments.ts** — CRUD handlers with taskId filtering and notifications to assignees and project members
- **src/handlers/notifications.ts** — List (with userId filter) and mark-as-read handlers
- **src/server.ts** — Wires up all routes and creates the HTTP server
- **src/main.ts** — Entry point reading PORT from env
- **src/demo.ts** — 34-step end-to-end demo covering every feature including error cases, cascade deletes, status transition enforcement, and notification flows

## Key Features
- All 22 API routes implemented as specified
- Status transitions enforced: `todo→in-progress→done` only (returns HTTP 422 on invalid)
- Notifications generated for: task assignment (at creation and via assign endpoint), status changes, and new comments
- Cascade deletes: deleting a project removes its tasks and comments; deleting a task removes its comments
- Input validation with meaningful error messages (400 for bad input, 404 for not found, 409 for conflicts, 422 for invalid transitions)
- Zero npm runtime dependencies — only Node.js built-ins (`http`, `crypto`, `url`)
